exposure: Women with one or more vaginal deliveries
Women with one or more Cesarean sections
outcome: Pelvic floor biometry (bladder neck, cervix, anorectal junction position, hiatal area)
cohort: 240 women out of 328 invited, who had undergone translabial ultrasound during their first singleton pregnancy and at 8 weeks and 1 year postpartum
finding: Compared to measurements at first trimester and 1 year postpartum, women had a lower bladder neck, cervix, and anorectal junction, and a greater hiatal area at 3-5 years after their first delivery, regardless of parity or mode of delivery.
mod_finding: Women with two or more vaginal deliveries had a greater hiatal area compared to those with only one, and women with at least one vaginal delivery had a greater hiatal area than those who had only Cesarean deliveries.
